transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to meet. As you know, next Thursday we'll be conducting our student-family reunification exercise following a simulated building evacuation. Before I can sign off on the final operating plan and we send the notice to families, I need to check in with each of you per our planning routine. The current draft has the gymnasium as our reunification site, a single transportation wave, an on-site medication table, and English-only pickup forms. I'd like to go around the room and hear from each of you — nurse, facilities, transportation, and family liaison — so we can identify any concerns or gaps before I approve the plan. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to start, Dr. Vega. While reviewing student health plans this week, I identified four students whose emergency medications must remain in temperature-controlled storage at all times. The only approved storage location during the exercise is the refrigerator in my office. However, the current draft plan still lists an on-site medication table at the gymnasium, which would not meet the temperature-controlled storage requirement for these students' medications. We need to address this gap before the plan is finalized.

transcript.text: Dr. Vega, I'd like to raise a concern as well. My family contact review, which I completed this week, shows that Spanish and Somali are the two additional languages needed for pickup instructions among our families. The current draft plan only provides English-only pickup forms, but the plan must provide pickup forms in English, Spanish, and Somali, and we need to have an interpreter available. These language-access details have not yet been entered into the draft, and this is a gap that needs to be addressed before the plan is finalized.

transcript.text: Dr. Vega, I need to raise an urgent facilities concern. I confirmed this week that the gymnasium floor will be sealed and inaccessible next Thursday from 7:00 a.m. through the end of the exercise. I received the facilities work-order confirmation, but this closure has not yet been added to the exercise plan. The cafeteria is the approved alternate reunification site, so we need to update the plan to use the cafeteria instead of the gymnasium before it's finalized.

transcript.text: Dr. Vega, I need to raise a transportation concern. I confirmed this week that the exercise group includes 96 students, but the school has only one available 50-seat bus because the second bus is assigned to another school. Transportation policy therefore requires exactly two bus waves to move all 96 students safely. However, the current draft plan still assumes only one transportation wave, and this gap needs to be corrected before the plan is finalized.

Would you like to direct how these updates are incorporated into the revised plan?

commitments.detail: Update the reunification site from the gymnasium to the cafeteria in the final operating plan.
Replace the on-site medication table at the gymnasium with temperature-controlled storage in the nurse's office refrigerator for the four identified students' emergency medications.
Update the transportation plan from one wave to two waves: first wave 50 students, second wave 46 students, with timing accounting for the round trip.
Provide pickup forms in English, Spanish, and Somali, and arrange for an interpreter to be available on-site during the exercise.
Once all four updates are incorporated into the revised draft, Dr. Vega will sign the final operating plan so the exercise notice can be sent to families.
